entries.title: Man, 53, shot inside West Englewood home
entries.summary: <p>A man was critically injured after being shot while inside a home in West Englewood Thursday night, according to Chicago police.</p><p>The man, 53, was at a residence in the 6900 block of South Oakley Avenue he wasn’t authorized to be in at 7:24 p.m. when a 46-year-old man shot him in the chest, police said. He was taken to Christ Medical Center in critical condition.</p><p>No one is in custody. The circumstances of the shooting are under investigation, police said. </p>

entries.title: The top matchups from the first round of football playoffs
entries.summary: <p><b>Class 5A</b></p><p><b>No. 24 Providence at No. 18 Kankakee</b></p><p><b>1 p.m. Saturday: </b>Kankakee (7-2) has only one loss on the field — 22-14 vs. No. 1 Lincoln-Way East; the Kays had to forfeit a win against Lincoln-Way West for using an ineligible player. Senior Phillip Turner is an electric dual-threat quarterback who has 1,691 total yards and 22 touchdowns with five interceptions. Sophomore Davion White is a playmaker on both sides of the ball. Providence (7-3) has a prolific offense led by running backs Broden Mackert and Brayden McKay along with quarterback Dominic Vita. The Celtics are 2-3 since interim coach Adam Nissen took over when Tyler Plantz was fired. They played eight playoff qualifiers in the regular season, losing to Mount Carmel, Nazareth and St. Ignatius.</p><p><b>Class 8A</b></p><p><b>Barrington at No. 14 Sandburg</b></p><p><b>7 p.m. Friday: </b>Barrington (6-4) has won six in a row after starting 0-4 against Lyons, Lincoln-Way Central, Naperville North and Hersey. Lamar Osterhues is one of the area’s top running backs with 1,282 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns. Sandburg (7-2) is looking for its first playoff win in 16 years. The Eagles can move the ball on the ground with Army recruit Quinn Durkin or through the air with quarterback Sean Ruisz and tight end Lucas Matykiewicz (Northern Illinois).</p><p><b>Class 8A</b></p><p><b>Glenbrook South</b></p><p><b> at No. 19 New Trier</b></p><p><b>6:30 p.m. Friday: </b>This is the teams’ second matchup in three weeks; New Trier won the first 35-28, also at home. Junior quarterback Liam Kearney of Glenbrook South (6-4) had 280 total yards and two passing touchdowns in the earlier loss. New Trier quarterback Jackie Ryder, a Purdue commit, has accounted for 2,006 total yards while playing just 26 quarters as the Trevians (8-1) won six games by 32 or more points. Their only loss was 35-28 to Maine South.</p><p><b>Class 7A</b></p><p><b>St. Laurence at Plainfield South</b></p><p><b>1 p.m. Saturday: </b>A year after reaching the Class 6A semifinals, St. Laurence (4-6) got into this year’s expanded playoff field as a 39th seed and went on the road to beat Belleville East 25-16 last week. Noah Taylor passed for one touchdown and ran for another for the Vikings, who have Illinois-bound linebacker Sean Rice back from an ankle injury. Plainfield South (8-1) won the Southwest Prairie East and lost only to Oswego. Sophomore quarterback Armani Ford has completed 64% of his passes for 2,429 yards and 19 touchdowns with four interceptions for the Cougars, whose last playoff win was in 2010.</p><p><b>Class 6A</b></p><p><b>Joliet Catholic at</b></p><p><b> Wheaton-Warrenville South</b></p><p><b>7 p.m. Friday: </b>Joliet Catholic (6-4) has one of the area’s best two-way players in senior linebacker/running back Derrick Pomatto, who has 82 tackles and 732 rushing yards with 10 touchdowns. The Hilltoppers closed the regular season with losses to Mount Carmel and IC Catholic before beating Bradley-Bourbonnais 44-3 in the opening round last week. Junior quarterback AJ Rogers has passed for more than 2,000 yards for Wheaton-Warrenville South (6-3), whose only loss since mid-September was 27-24 to Batavia.</p>

entries.title: FDA issues alert about Northfield-based Medline beds tied to fire-related deaths and injuries
entries.summary: <p>The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an alert about Northfield-based medical supply company Medline’s beds Thursday after two people died and 16 others were seriously injured by the product.</p><p>The FDA issued an <a class="Link" href="https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/medical-device-recalls-and-early-alerts/early-alert-medline-removes-or-corrects-all-medline-brand-beds-and-accessories" target="_blank" ><u>Early Alert warning</u></a> Thursday about Medline beds for patients in home or long-term care — as well as their accessories, such as mattresses, side rails and more — citing a potential fire hazard. Medline issued its own alert earlier this month saying it was removing the product from sale and exiting the market for the beds.</p><p>The beds’ electrical components have the potential to overheat, causing the casing to melt and produce smoke or cause fires, and the related accessories have the potential to entrap or asphyxiate patients, per the alert. As of Oct. 20, the company said it was aware of at least two deaths and 16 injuries related to the products.</p><p>“We believe this action best supports our commitment to product quality and safety for healthcare providers and the patients and communities they serve,” the company said in a statement. “We recognize the impact this decision may have on the healthcare system. Medline is taking actions to support affected customers and healthcare providers and to help minimize disruption while prioritizing patient safety.”</p><p>For current product owners, Medline says they can still be used, but suggests only plugging in the beds to reposition the patient and not to use extension cords to power them.</p><p>Some of the beds may be able to be repaired, according to the alert, though those that aren’t will be eligible for a full refund or replacement.</p><p>Customers can call Medline recall customer service line at 1-800-950-0128 and choose option No. 7 to start the process. Customers can also report any adverse events, such as fires, to the FDA <a class="Link" href="https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/medwatch/index.cfm" target="_blank" ><u>online</u></a>.</p><p>“The FDA is currently reviewing information about this potentially high-risk device issue and will keep the public informed as significant new information becomes available,” the agency said in a statement.</p>

entries.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams fined again for wearing cleats
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> quarterback Caleb Williams will continue wearing Caddix cleats, and the NFL will keep fining him.</p><p>One week after he was first fined $11,941 for wearing the cleats against the Falcons — specifically, for showing a logo that wasn’t Nike, Adidas or Under Armour on game day — Williams was fined for donning them against the Patriots, a source confirmed. ESPN reported Williams was fined twice as much as he was for initial transgression: $23,882.</p><p>Williams had expected to be fined. He <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/28/bears-quarterback-caleb-williams-caddix-cleats-nfl-fine-keeping-wearing" target="_blank" >said Wednesday</a> he’d continue wearing the cleats, which claim to reduce stress on players’ joints.</p><p>“I’m focused on being able to be out here for the guys,” Williams said. “And if that can give me a small percentage up [as a fine] and it works, then that’s what I’m gonna do.”</p><p>Williams was not fined earlier in the season when he wore all-white Caddix cleats without a prominent logo. About 40 NFL players have worn them in a game. Caddix co-founder Jack Rasmussen told the Sun-Times this week he'd be "happy to cover his fines."</p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Blackhawks lose to Red Wings as 'pretty much everything' goes wrong
entries.summary: <p>DETROIT — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> coach Jeff Blashill struck a relatively positive tone after many of his team's first eight losses this season, sometimes to a surprising degree considering what the games looked like.</p><p>But after the ninth loss — a 4-1 defeat Thursday against the Red Wings that was more lopsided than the score suggested — there was no positive rhetoric to be found.</p><p>"We've had a lot of games throughout this season where we did a lot of good things and maybe beat ourselves with critical mistakes," Blashill said. "Tonight, to me, wasn't that at all. It's a step backwards. Because you just had too many guys that weren't skating, didn't compete hard enough or [didn't have] enough attention to detail."</p><p>The result kept the Hawks winless on the road (0-5) and squandered their hopes of building momentum from what might've been their best team-wide performance Tuesday against the Kings.</p><p>Maybe the Hawks were still bloated from a festive dinner Wednesday that kicked off the team's biennial "dad's trip." Maybe the Red Wings were extra motivated to prove they don't need Dylan Larkin after the latest dramatic twist in his trade-request saga.</p><p>Or maybe the Hawks as currently constructed — and/or as currently coached — have no chance of sustaining success. The answer remains to be seen. But there was plenty of hand-wringing in the locker room.</p><p>"Overall, it was a pretty poor effect," Ian Cole said. "All of us expected to use Tuesday’s game to springboard us into a string of good play. It was pretty unfortunate we did what we did tonight."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Wings goal: Arvidsson pushes in his second of the game. <a href="https://t.co/ESV8Sel9N8">pic.twitter.com/ESV8Sel9N8</a></p>— BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) <a href="https://x.com/BlackhawksFocus/status/2115986098446897499?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 30, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Patrick Kane's son Trick was at Little Caesar's Arena for his dad's strangely emotional welcome back to Detroit — coming less than three years after his extremely emotional, memorable welcome back to Chicago — but Kane followed that up with a poor night on the ice.</p><p>The Wings outshot the Hawks 10-4 and outscored them 2-0 during Kane's five-on-five ice time, and his seventh minor penalty of the season led to the Wings' go-ahead power-play goal early in the third period.</p><p>Kane said "pretty much everything" went wrong and acknowledged he needs to cut down on his penalties.</p><p>"[It] seems like a lot of them are [me] trying to lift a stick and either getting caught in the hands or high-sticking," he said. "I'll be better in that area."</p>
